name: Firefox Add-ons (AMO)

sources.title: Extension Workshop — 'Submitting an add-on' doc hub (Listing on AMO vs self-distribution)

requirements: Only applicable if the product ships a real Firefox extension/theme — this is a browser add-on store, not a web-app directory
Extension must be packaged as a zip/xpi and pass Mozilla's automated validation and signing
Listed submissions are reviewed against the Add-on Policies (Submission Guidelines, content, data-collection disclosure, monetization rules)
Two distribution paths: 'Listing on AMO' (public directory listing) or self-distribution (signed but unlisted, hosted on your own site)
preparation: A working WebExtension (manifest.json, packaged .zip) — use web-ext build/lint first
A Firefox Account for the AMO Developer Hub
Listing assets: name, icon, summary, description, screenshots, category, keywords/tags
Source code upload ready if the extension uses minified/obfuscated code (source code submission rules)
Decision on listed (AMO public page) vs unlisted/self-distributed signing
workflow: Register/sign in to the AMO Developer Hub at addons.mozilla.org with a Firefox Account
Choose 'Submit a New Add-on' and pick On this site (listed) vs self-distribution
Upload the packaged add-on; wait for automated validation/signing checks
Fill the listing metadata (name, summary, description, categories, screenshots, support links)
Submit for review; fix any reviewer-reported policy issues
After approval the public AMO listing page goes live
watchFor: Manual review required for listed add-ons — obfuscated or bundled third-party code triggers source-code requests
Requesting broad/unnecessary permissions slows review; justify permissions in review notes
A rejected submission can leave the add-on signed-but-unlisted; check Developer Hub status, not just the upload receipt
AMO outbound links are nofollow — treat this as a distribution channel, not an SEO link
countsAsLive: The add-on has a public, indexable listing page on addons.mozilla.org with an 'Add to Firefox' install button
unknowns: Whether a SaaS without a browser extension has any valid route (none found — extension required)
